bound_context.question: What does the 97-byte leaf routine at 0x62ad5e0 return for a splits pointer and a count, and what do its callers depend on?

caller_census.method: Capstone disassembly of the artifact; each call site validated at the instruction boundary and attributed to the .eh_frame FDE that encloses it

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (19 anchors: claim -> target instruction address, bytes and decoded instruction)
environment_limits: Static only: the artifact was never executed, and no source build is claimed.
The model executes the routine's decoded bytes on a small machine model that implements exactly the instructions present and raises on any other; it is not a general x86 emulator.
capstone 5.0.7 / readelf / objdump were used; results are reproducible with those tools on the digest-verified binary.
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 75 per family over empty/single/pairs/odd); the full 2,400-case sweep and a 3,000-array random differential are re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: From the disassembly: rdi = splits, esi = n, and the sum is returned in rax; the routine reads splits but never writes memory.
test %esi,%esi at 0x62ad5e4 followed by je 0x62ad638 at 0x62ad5e6, where xor %eax,%eax at 0x62ad638 zeroes the result: an empty slice returns 0 without touching splits.

cmp $0x1,%esi with je 0x62ad63b (0x62ad5e8/0x62ad5eb) sends n == 1 to xor %esi,%esi / xor %eax,%eax / jmp (0x62ad63b..0x62ad63f), which lands on the SAME scalar add at 0x62ad62c; the routine therefore contains exactly one scalar add from memory.

shr $1,%edx (0x62ad5f6), shl $0x4,%rdx and add %rdi,%rdx (0x62ad5fa/0x62ad5fc) build end = splits + 16*(n>>1); the loop body at 0x62ad600 loads 16 bytes (movdqu) and adds them with paddq, advancing rax by 16 until it equals rdx.
paddq adds two 64-bit lanes with no carry between them, and the horizontal fold (movdqa/psrldq $0x8/paddq at 0x62ad611..0x62ad61a) is another paddq, so the result is the sum modulo 2**64.
movq %xmm0,%rax at 0x62ad61e keeps only the low 64-bit lane of the folded accumulator, which is what makes the result a 64-bit wrap.

test $0x1,%sil with je (0x62ad623/0x62ad627) skips the tail for an even count; for an odd count and $0xfffffffe,%esi (0x62ad629) forms the index n & ~1 and add (%rdi,%rsi,8),%rax (0x62ad62c) adds that element AFTER the horizontal fold.
The body is a leaf: no calls, no stores, no relocations, and the whole body is one .eh_frame FDE 0x62ad5e0..0x62ad641 (97 bytes, 32 instructions).
3 direct calls, 0 tail jumps, all three inside the single caller FDE 0x62ac520..0x62ac9c9; two consumers copy the sum out of rax and one stores it, so no call site discards the result.

Reading the 8-byte elements as size_t and the result as the byte total of the slice follows from the mangled name and from the callers' use of the value; the packet does not prove the C++ level type beyond that.
Reading the callers as zstd's COVER cost evaluation is inferred from the enclosing object (cover.o) and the symbol name; the surrounding function is not reconstructed here.

unknowns: The C-level meaning of the count at each call site and whether it is ever zero or one in practice; the routine handles both, but the callers' runtime arguments are not characterized here.
What each caller does with the sum beyond its first read (the consumer class is recorded, the downstream arithmetic is not).
The alignment of the splits array at run time is not observable statically; the routine uses an unaligned load (movdqu), so it is alignment-independent.
The body is byte-identical in 3 identical source objects; only 0x62ad5e0 is bound.
